source: GSE156243, the deposit of the 2021 organoid paper (PMID 34268881); exploratory set-level analysis by scientist-c

EXPLORATORY NEGATIVES: transcripts are not PDH activity, flux or metabolite, and do not show that PDH or lactate are normal.

source: GSE156243 (deposit of PMID 34268881); unplanned descriptive reading in this package
note: IL6 0 counts in all six libraries; IL1B 0-11; TNF 0-1; P2RY12 0: no cytokine-expressing compartment. NFE2L2 0.75x, KEAP1 0.93x, NQO1 0.73x, G6PD 0.75x, SLC7A11 0.65x, BACH1 0.73x; HMOX1 1.67x, SRXN1 1.33x, GSR 1.20x: no coherent NRF2 signature. Design (IT11 P2.3 verification, deposit and paper read): WT is one parental line; the 2 WT libraries are the survivors of a post hoc exclusion (one low-quality, one non-clustering); KO clone and batch are not assigned in the deposit; only NFE2L2 is in the authors' DE list (padj 1.43E-02, log2FC -0.58, above the stated alpha 0.01); NQO1 0.73x and HMOX1 1.67x are in neither list. NFE2L2 and NQO1 transcripts are lower in all four KO libraries (the arm-R-compatible direction) while HMOX1, SRXN1 and GSR are higher (the adaptive direction): descriptive, not a test.

source: GSE156243 (PMID 34268881 deposit); descriptive panel by scientist-c, disease-models/wwox/research/drug_repurposing/w2_therapeutic_it2_20261027/README.md
note: PDGFRA and OLIG1 are nominally higher in knockouts, SOX10, MOG and OLIG2 are not; counts are very low and composition differs; a week-15 organoid has no compact myelin. Not myelin evidence.

source: GSE156243 (the deposit of PMID 34268881), descriptive panel by scientist-a
note: Microglial markers are at or near zero (P2RY12, CX3CR1, PTPRC, TREM2) so the tissue cannot test a microglial arm; of seven reactive-pan genes above 5 CPM only VIM and CD44 are raised (both radial-glia or progenitor associated), SERPINA3, TIMP1 and SOCS3 are lower, C3 and STAT3 not separated; IL1B, IL6, TNF are not informative (under 20 raw counts). Not a gliosis measurement and not myelin or seizure evidence.

source: GSE156243, the deposit of the 2021 organoid paper (PMID 34268881); descriptive extraction in the IT9 P4c-e package (organoid_target_gene_rows.tsv); not an evaluation by reversal of any gene set
note: EPAS1 3.80 times, HK2 4.73 times, SLC2A1 2.67 times, ARNT 1.46 times; HIF1A mRNA 0.84 times (flat, as expected for a protein-level axis); PDK1 0.78 times. Four versus two libraries, one laboratory; the glycolytic genes also fall with elapsed culture time in unperturbed spheroids, so composition or maturity can contribute. IT10 P2.1 (premises a2, a3): the elevation is selective, a partly canonical hypoxia-response pattern and not a uniform glycolytic upshift (ADM, HK2, P4HA1, SLC2A1, BHLHE40, ANKRD37, EGLN3, DDIT4 up; PGK1, ALDOA, ENO1, PKM, PFKP, NDRG1, CA9 flat), compatible with HIF activity, with oxygen limitation of the organoid and with MYC (MYC +0.56 log2); the knockout's offsets in 12 progenitor and neuronal marker genes predict only a small maturity-related shift (median +0.08 to +0.16 log2 for HK2, SLC2A1, LDHA) against the observed +2.18, +1.40 and +0.75, which makes marker-measured maturity a minor contributor but does not exclude composition by unmeasured subpopulations or culture state (exploratory, calibration from another laboratory). HK2, SLC2A1 and PDK1 belong to the six-gene IT7 readout (guard IT7_READOUT6): they are observations here and cannot be used to evaluate any compound.

source: GSE156243 (deposit of PMID 34268881), set-level and gene-level re-analysis by scientist-c; wwox_systems_comparison_it5_20261029.md section 2
note: PDK1 -0.39, LOWER IN SIGN ONLY: inside the single-gene null (p about 0.30), so the datum is the absence of support for a raised PDK1, not a demonstrated decrease (the earlier card E03 prints -0.34 for the same comparison; the two runs differ in method and the difference is not reconciled here). The PDK set as a whole is indistinguishable from chance. Transcript, not PDK protein, PDH phosphorylation or activity. The maturity confound of this deposit applies.

The 'near-complete rescue at high dose, partial at low dose' is the authors' sentence on representative micrographs; no treated-arm quantification, no untreated-knockout column in that panel, no g-ratio or electron microscopy. The oligodendrocyte-promoter vector gave no detectable WWOX, so that arm does not test oligodendroglial relevance.

source: Obeid 2026 (PMID 42422765), AAV9 study: P10 untreated knockout about 95 against wild type about 130 (manifest figure attestation); abstract-level statement re-read in this cycle from the local JATS: neuronal-promoter vectors rescue hypoglycaemia; the 2014 WWOX and HIF1alpha paper, abstract: Wwox-deficient mice 'succumb to a lethal hypoglycemia early in life'
note: Two laboratories, two ages, very different magnitudes (about 95 against 130 at P10 in one study; about 10 against 130 in the other, a Figure 1 reading carried from the manifest and not re-opened). Hypoglycaemia is rescued by a neuronal-promoter vector; strong ubiquitous promoters rescued it early only (the paper says the protection was not sustained at later stages); an oligodendrocyte promoter and the weak ubiquitous promoter did not (JATS text read), so it is not a purely peripheral readout. UNVERIFIABLE_SURFACE for the blind audit: both figure readings (about 95 against 130; about 10 against 130) are carried from manifests, and the sentence quoted from the 2014 abstract is a background statement about earlier work, not a result of that paper; but the null dies early, so the endpoint is survivor-conditioned and confounded with feeding, seizures and growth (NEED-SYSTEMIC-GLYCAEMIA-GROWTH).

source: Tochigi 2019 (PMID 31340538) Figure 6D; Repudi 2021 (PMID 33914858) Figure 1J-O and Supplementary Figure 1
note: No Wwox signal was seen in Iba1-positive microglia by that assay; astrocyte-specific deletion was scored for delay, weight and survival (control 8, knockout 9) with no abnormality, and the paper does not report GFAP or Iba1 immunoreactivity, EEG or seizures for it; the authors say a cell-autonomous astroglial function is not excluded.

source: PMID 42909904 (Lucas-Clarke 2026), Results (Figure 5F and G), Methods (imaging of the sima:GFP reporter) and supplementary stock table
note: No change (t = 0.6623, P = 0.5185, N = 7 to 9 brains; amyloid background, one genotype pair, normoxia, not measured without the transgene or under hypoxia). The reporter's identity is internally inconsistent in the paper: the Results (and legend) say 'endogenously tagged sima:GFP', the Methods name 'the genetically encoded reporter line UAS-sima:GFP' (a driver-expressed transgene, whose level reports protein stability and not transcription), and the stock table lists a GFP-tagged sima PBac line (BDSC 42672). Sima is the single fly HIF-alpha, so no HIF-1 versus HIF-2 split is possible. The authors attribute the lactate rise to Atf4, not to sima. The only neural HIF-alpha protein readout in a WWOX-loss model, invertebrate, and not evidence of absence in mammals.

source: PMID 42397075, Results and Fig 3J-K; knockout, WOREE-derived and SCAR12-derived organoids
note: Higher in all three mutant lines (box medians read by eye: wild type about 18, knockout about 68, SCAR12 about 45, WOREE about 55 percent, wide scatter). SCAR12 overlaps the wild-type lower tail. Protein-level, small organoid numbers, one laboratory. In SCAR12 the radial-glia fraction is wild-type-like and the single-cell neuron-cluster fraction is not reduced (DA-M01-003; WOREE shows reduced CTIP2 and SATB2, Fig 6B, so SCAR12 is the clean dissociation case), so the MYC rise is present without that composition phenotype.

source: PAPER 031 (Breton 2021, neuron-specific Wwox knockout mouse slices)
note: Amplitude shifted up in knockout (cumulative distributions, KS test on pooled events; 10 cells per genotype from 4 wild-type, 5 heterozygote and 5 knockout animals); frequency is not different from the heterozygote but does differ from wild type (KS P about 2.4e-4; direction not stated in the text); decay time constant not different, which the authors read as no overt change of the NMDAR:AMPA proportion. INFERENZA (the producer's, not the paper's): at the -70 mV holding potential NMDAR current is largely magnesium-blocked, so the recording is probably AMPAR-weighted; a residual NMDAR component is not excluded and no NMDAR current was measured.

source: Hussain 2023 (PMID 36828035), Results 2.5
note: Declared 'data not shown': an unverifiable negative that may not be cited as evidence that the heterozygote has no gliosis.

source: Hussain 2019 (PMID 30290271), Figures 3 and 4
note: Area fraction, not cell number; dentate gyrus unmarked; Il6 and Tnf-a transcripts both about 1.5-fold or more up by qPCR (n 4 per group), but only Il6 reaches p below 0.05: Results 3.3 reads '( Il6 significant at p < .05)', and Fig 4E shows Il6 about 1.48x with one asterisk and Tnf-a about 1.85x with a large error bar and no mark; full text re-read 2026-10-31 (IT10 P2.2, publisher text and figure image), which restores the original registry reading 'Il6 but not Tnf-a' and corrects the 2026-10-30 'correction' that had dropped the word Il6; the authors' own abstract and Discussion nevertheless state that both cytokines are increased, which their significance mark does not support; the paper records no seizure measurement for these animals and leaves cause versus consequence open.

source: PMID 33914858 (Repudi 2021, Brain), Results and Fig 1; text read in the operator-supplied copy
note: Both progenitor-stage (nestin-Cre) and neuron-stage (Synapsin-Cre) deletion reproduce growth retardation, seizures and premature death (death by four weeks is stated for nestin-Cre; the Synapsin-Cre survival age is not stated); that progenitors are largely WWOX-intact under Synapsin-Cre is an inference, not a measurement; oligodendrocyte and astrocyte deletion do not. Radial-glia state and MYC were not measured in these mice, and the mouse cortex is not the human outer-radial-glia system.

source: Hussain 2019 (PMID 30290271), Results 3.3, Fig 4E (publisher HTML PMC7104842 and repo XML)
note: 'We observed > 1.5 fold upregulation of both cytokines ( Il6 significant at p < .05)': significance is attached to Il6 only; the figure shows Il6 about 1.48x with one asterisk and Tnf-a about 1.85x with a large error bar and no mark. Il6 is the only significant cytokine; Tnf-a is a non-significant increase. This corrects the IT9 P1 'correction' that dropped the word Il6. The authors' abstract and Discussion state that both cytokines are increased; the method is a two-tailed unpaired Student's t, Gapdh, 2-week-old KO versus Cre-positive littermates, n 4 v 4; absence of a significance mark is not absence of an effect.

source: GSE126075 (deposit of PMID 31543760), descriptive P6 run, one library per arm; wwox_systems_comparison_it5_20261029.md section 2
note: Progenitors -0.67, LOWER IN SIGN ONLY: inside the single-gene null (p about 0.49) and the interval (about 0.45, Poisson) spans zero; the day-14 neuron stage shows +0.44 (same interval), so the sign is not concordant across stages and no decrease is demonstrated. n = 1 per arm: descriptive only. The progenitor line also differs in state from its control (radial-glia markers lower), which confounds every metabolic comparison in it.

source: PMID 35328751 (Baryla 2022): the same polyclonal WWOX sgRNA fibroblast pool; fractionated blot, 6 h, one repetition shown
note: Cytoplasmic HIF-1alpha is LOWER in two of four conditions (about two-fold in normoxia with normoglycaemia, p below 0.01, and nearly two-fold in hypoxia with normoglycaemia, p below 0.001); no significant difference is reported for the other two; one blot repetition is shown. It is the cytoplasmic pool, whereas the MEF increase is nuclear: different compartments, so this neither confirms nor cleanly contradicts the MEF observation.

source: PMID 35328751 (Baryla 2022): the same polyclonal WWOX sgRNA fibroblast pool; fractionated blot
note: The Results say, verbatim, "We didn't observed WWOX influence on HIF1α protein in nuclear fraction": no difference was observed (the authors' wording; not a demonstrated equivalence). The authors' Discussion nevertheless states that WWOX knock-out leads to increased HIF1A mRNA and protein together with its translocation to the nucleus, which their own fractionated blot does not show; what survives of that sentence is the HRE reporter and mRNA result (DA-K01-003).

source: Baryla 2022 (PMID 35328751), Figure 5b and Results; carried through needs NEED-PDH-PYRUVATE-AXIS observation O2; Results sentence re-read in this cycle
note: A null is NO_CHANGE, not proof of normal PDH regulation: n is not stated and PDH phosphorylation is not measured. Wording flag found in this cycle: one Results sentence lists 'pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase (PDK)' among the enzymes whose activity was unchanged, while Methods describe only a PDH kit and Figure 5b is labelled PDH; the repository reads it as the PDH assay (manifest entries 7 and 8); not resolved by the paper. PDH is named as unchanged in the normoxia-hyperglycaemia and hypoxia-normoglycaemia sentences; for hypoxia-hyperglycaemia the text says no effect on enzyme activities. In the same cells hexokinase activity, LDH activity and lactate were higher.

source: Karnstedt 2026, Epilepsia (PMID 41489401, PMC13075606; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE; other disease)
note: Benefit in 14 of 19 individuals with gain-of-function variants, of whom 4 had an effect that faded (10 sustained; at variant level counting sustained effect only the authors report P = 0.0698, not significant) (behaviour 12 of 17, development 6 of 12, seizure frequency reduced in 7 of 18); three gain-of-function individuals worsened. Retrospective, unblinded, clinician or parent rated.

source: Karnstedt 2026, Epilepsia (PMID 41489401; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE; other disease)
note: Benefit in 3 of 15 (group of 15 includes 4 non-pathogenic variants), mild and parent-reported only; seizure reduction 2 of 10, not different from the gain-of-function group. The direction of the receptor lesion, not the presence of an NMDAR gene, separated responders.

source: Teplyshova 2024, Front Genet (PMID 39507621), as recorded in analysis/downstream_wwox_independent_rescue_census_20260921.md W2.5; the drug effect is NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (n = 1, polytherapy)
note: 'No sustained positive effect of treatment was detected' for the whole list taken over decades in one adult; the drug is not isolated, the exposure and timing are unknown. n = 1 supports no statement about the drug in this genotype.

source: PMIDs 24889205 (DMOG versus KC7F2 in rat seizure models), 42276303 (HIF-1alpha overexpression), 34021541 (miR-485 acting on HDAC5, HIF1alpha and PFKFB3), abstracts; PMID 36655171 (activity raises LDHA through AMPK and HIF-1alpha), targeted full text; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: Two-sided: a HIF agonist (DMOG) delayed epileptogenesis in the chronic phase and an inhibitor did the opposite, with no acute effect; HIF-1alpha overexpression raised CaV3.2 promoter activity and network firing; lowering HIF-1alpha, HDAC5 and PFKFB3 together accompanied fewer seizures; chronic neuronal activity itself raises LDHA through AMPK and HIF-1alpha. A glycolytic shift in a hyperactive network need not be WWOX-dependent. Abstract level for most rows; both agonist and inhibitor are non-selective. (abstract level; HIF gain of function raises firing in cultured neurons; mediation by CaV3.2 is not tested in the abstract, although the authors' closing sentence is causal; no WWOX to CACNA link found)

ROS substantially higher in late-passage nulls, no difference in early passage; early-passage redox-homeostasis transcripts (including Nfe2l2, Nqo1 per the manifest; one sample per genotype) are higher; NAC rescues senescence escape. Non-neural; an initial antioxidant response is suggested by the authors as an open question.

source: Gupta 2023, PMID 37319242 (Results 'Low dose/long-duration studies'); NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: No significant difference in homocysteine or activity; a very slight rise in protein in some animals and no Hsp70 induction. The regulatory-domain allele that was rescued at high exposure (DR-A02-004) was therefore not rescued at tolerated exposure (PMID 37319242, Results 'Low dose/long-duration studies', last paragraph).

source: Guiberson 2018 (PMID 30266908), Supplementary Figure 12a, mutant panel read in IT5 P8; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: Mutant total protein about 1.05 of untreated control, no significance mark (three experiments); the text lists only the phenylbutyrate class and two osmolytes as stabilising. On wild type the same comparator gave a scattered, unmarked value near 1.95. The comparator was more potent than the phenylbutyrate class on class-I HDAC enzymes in one ChEMBL document but weaker on HDAC1 in a third that also lists the sodium salt, so that premise is document-dependent; it does not engage HDAC6 at the applied level; no pan-HDAC or HDAC6-selective arm exists in this paper. A measured null in a cell that is not comparable.

source: Gupta 2023, PMID 37319242 (Results, sentence on Tg-T191M); NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: Neither inhibitor restored significant activity ('a very small amount' with bortezomib). The same allele gained activity with bortezomib in a human kidney-line model (DR-A02-008), so the allele does not fix the outcome: expression context and readout differ. A measured null in this system. The HEK paper's own summary of the mouse work says bortezomib partially rescued I278T and T191M, which is more generous than the mouse paper's wording; the mouse paper's wording is used here.

source: Gupta 2023, PMID 37319242 (Results 'Low dose/long-duration studies'); NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: With tolerated exposure the activity gain was not significant and a white-cell and lymphocyte reduction was still present; homocysteine fell by about half (mean 345 to 179 micromolar, significant linear trend) yet stayed far above normal, with no significant activity gain, and one of eight treated animals had the largest response and was also the one with the greatest weight loss and lowest white-cell counts. The authors conclude that proteasome inhibitors are probably not feasible as monotherapy at non-toxic exposure.

source: independent Fanconi-anaemia study (known-roads reading 2, 40544182); NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: MEASURED NO PHENOTYPIC RESCUE (survival, aberrations, micronuclei) and NMD not relieved, while full-length protein was induced in one arm (FANCA, about 9 percent of control) and not in the other; the endpoint encoded here is the phenotypic rescue only, so the protein induction is stated in this note and not in the direction code; the effect that was seen is attributed by the authors to TBK1/IKKe inhibition, not read-through. Encoded NO_CHANGE for the phenotypic endpoint.

source: Ann Clin Transl Neurol 2026 prospective cohort (PMID 41288262; abstract only; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)
note: Adult safety signal reassuring but non-randomised; it bears on the warning, not on children, not on a developmental epilepsy and not on benefit.

source: JAMA Netw Open 2026 randomised trial abstract, PMID 42771346; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: Ratio 1.04 (95 percent credible interval 0.83 to 1.32) over a 24-week placebo-controlled period: no benefit despite target engagement and proof of mechanism in the earlier phase. Adults with ALS; says nothing about a developmental encephalopathy.

source: J Alzheimers Dis 2026 abstract, PMID 42179084; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: Better recognition memory and less microglial activation and tau; amyloid burden not reduced; p-eIF2 alpha lower. Mouse, adult, 23 days, one study.

source: Alekseeva 2026, Biomedicines (PMID 42652189; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE; adult rat, acute provoked seizures), as recorded in the repository
note: Memantine accelerated every seizure stage; perampanel delayed stage 4 but did not prevent seizures. The reading carries unresolved internal inconsistencies noted in that record. A safety-direction datum for a non-genetic model, not WWOX.

source: CPP-115 (a vigabatrin analogue), rat, PMID 24321005, abstract; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: CPP-115 only, not vigabatrin. The abstract states that spasm cessation was not accelerated and that neurodevelopmental behaviour and visuospatial learning were not altered; brain histology is not mentioned in the abstract.

source: vigabatrin, human neuropathology, PMID 1940119 and PMID 2767014; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: No microvacuolation or sheath splitting attributable to the drug was found, and no demyelination, in the 62 examined people; two post-mortem and three operative specimens showed no vacuolation. Abstract level, ages and exposure windows not stated; a negative in people who were not infants does not exclude the infant lesion the label records.

source: vigabatrin and GABA, rat cerebellar explant culture, PMID 2757909; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: Mild toxicity for myelinated fibres from vigabatrin and from GABA with no clear difference between them; no intramyelinic oedema and no primary demyelination were seen, so the row is not a vacuolation finding (its target is the in-vitro fibre endpoint). GABA alone reproduced the mild toxicity.

source: GABA-B agonists and GABA, mouse demyelination model and rat precursor cultures, PMID 35980256 and PMID 31349008; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: GABA-B engagement enhanced precursor differentiation, myelin protein and remyelination, and a GABA-A agonist did not reproduce the effect in the coculture study; the axis therefore has opposite signs by receptor class. Signalling studies, not drug exposures of a developing brain.

source: Sheeni 2026 (PMC13701765, PMID 42939870); NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: Different molecule; 'acute Nrf2 target engagement was not measured'; cytokine mRNA differences not significant at 10 weeks; MIXED-to-favourable, adult acquired epilepsy. Not transferable to omaveloxolone.

source: vigabatrin, human children aged 2 to 16 and adults, PMID 19054414; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: No statistically significant difference between exposed and naive subjects in the older bands (668 subjects); the age-band contrast within one study is what the row carries. A non-significant difference is not proof of no difference.

source: dichloroacetate, human children, Stacpoole 2006 (PMID 16651305), randomized double-blind trial (43 patients), abstract; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: A population in which lactate was persistently or intermittently raised, with a defined defect in most patients, and in which the lever still did not change the clinical outcomes measured over six months. Heterogeneous and short; a null in this design does not exclude a benefit in a defined genotype.

source: dichloroacetate, mouse, Durie 2018 (PMID 29913407), abstract; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: Target engagement was partial and the phospho-site did not move significantly; total PDH protein fell 23% in non-epileptic mice on treatment, which the authors offer as a possible reason for the pro-convulsant signal.

source: dichloroacetate, mouse, Durie 2018 (PMID 29913407), abstract; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: Chronic treatment before the test. One laboratory; the abstract reports no effect size.

source: dichloroacetate, mouse, Durie 2018 (PMID 29913407), abstract; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: The only primary seizure-endpoint test of a PDK inhibitor found in a model in which PDH activity is documented to be reduced. Abstract level; the full text is closed.

source: dichloroacetate, human fibroblasts, Simpson 2006 (PMID 16765624), abstract; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: The response to the PDK inhibitor depended on a pre-existing PDH defect: no significant effect in control cells (six patient lines and five control subjects; the 29% average excludes one patient line with an unusual splicing mutation). It supplies the design of the discriminating experiment (a genotype-by-inhibitor interaction on glucose-derived acetyl-CoA flux), with a precedent for what a responder looks like.

source: US prescribing information for vigabatrin oral solution (openFDA drug label JSON, version effective 2026-06-15, set id 082d818a-4f4e-4675-98c6-91db0294e63c), sections 5.3 and 5.4; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
note: Label sections 5.3, 5.4 and 8.4 and the boxed warning were read in full from the JSON; the cited study itself was not read, so the 22 and 4 percent figures are the label's statement of it. The label states that the specific pattern was not observed in older children and adults. Vigabatrin only. Section 5.3 also records postmarketing MRI changes in children 6 years and younger treated for refractory complex partial seizures. 22 percent is the prevalence in the vigabatrin-treated infants of that study (non-WWOX, infantile spasms) and 4 percent the comparator on other therapies; arm sizes are not in the label. Batch ORCH-SCIBATCH-DR-20261105 (B1): three independent centres put the rate among imaged children between 22.1 and 44.7 percent (one at partial full-text depth, the others at abstract level); the one cohort reporting its exposed denominator gives about 26 percent per exposed child; and unexposed comparators exist (7 of 52 in one cohort; 4 percent of naive infants in the controlled study). These are frequencies in selected cohorts, not attributable risk in WWOX.

source: openFDA drug label JSON for memantine, effective 2026-09-01, retrieved 2026-10-29 (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)
note: The only controlled paediatric exposure to memantine in the label is a null result in a different disorder.

source: GSE158681 and GSE158682 (P17 Wwox conditional and germline deletion brain; inputs identical to the IT6 P4 analysis by sha256), computed anew in IT10 P2.1; NOT the organoid
note: A COUNTER-OBSERVATION to the organoid rows: no elevation of HIF-axis or glycolysis transcripts in any of four contrasts; Hif1a within +-0.2 log2, Hk2 flat (-0.01 to +0.35), Epas1 lower (-0.21 to -0.58, animal-separated in 3 of 4), Slc2a1, Ldha and Pgk1 lower, Ndrg1 and P4ha1 lower in all four, Gfap higher. Caveats: bulk tissue and TPM; the animals come from lines with severe epilepsy and death at 3 to 4 weeks; background differences between control groups; no protein; gliosis and hypomyelination change composition. It does not side with the organoid: a species or in-vivo-versus-organoid disagreement is the largest unresolved fact of this axis. Exploratory, post hoc (IT10 P2.1 disclosure).
